description: A conformance suite of CexChain evidence (spec sections 11 and 15): each case is one evidence bundle (kind "record", verified as `cexchain verify` does) or one instance's contract evidence (kind "contract", as `cexchain contract verify` does), with the options to verify it with, the verdict the specification decides, and, for a failure, the section and step that decide it. tools/testvectors/evidence_suite.py forges every ledger from spec/README.md and spec/cexchain.cddl alone, independently of the C++ programs and of the Python verifier: statements signed with throwaway keys (seed = SHA-256("CexChain test key: evidence <name>"); Ed25519, ESP256, SM2 through the openssl command line, ML-DSA), log entries, state commitments, checkpoints, receipts, cosignatures, and anchors with RFC 3161 tokens by OpenSSL's responder (`openssl ts`), whose authorities' root and certificates `cryptography` makes (P-256, valid 2020-2040). Contract calls run the v0.6 oracle contract (oracle_contract in generate.py: a byte-string argument is its output) on the reference interpreter, wasm_ref.py, which must give the output each call was forged with. Options: `ledger_id` (the expected ledger, hex), `witnesses` (trusted witness keys, each the hex of a public key file, CBOR [alg, key]), `min_witnesses`, `tsa_roots` (trusted authorities' root certificates, PEM), `min_timestamps`, `attachments` (contents by name, hex), `require_presence` and `require_answered` (contract evidence only); an option left out is not used. A verifier must reach `verified`. When verified, its JSON report (the fields of `cexchain verify --json` or `cexchain contract verify --json`) must match `facts`, which hold only what was forged: a fact object matches a report object when every key of the fact is in the report and its value matches; a fact list matches a report list of the same length, element by element; any other value matches only an equal value (true, false, null, numbers, and strings exactly). Failures have no facts. Times in facts are the report's ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds; a token's time is its genTime and its accuracy one second. ECDSA, SM2, and ML-DSA signatures and the tokens' times differ from one run of the generator to the next; verdicts and facts do not.

cases.name: record-plain
cases.description: The organization registers a record; the bundle ends with the state commitment.

cases.name: record-plain-no-expected-ledger
cases.description: The same bundle verified without an expected ledger id: it verifies, unchecked against one.

cases.name: record-disclosures-attachment
cases.description: A person's record under a delegation: two of four fields disclosed, one of two attachments opened and checked against its content.

cases.name: record-agent-delegation-chain
cases.description: An AI agent, registered by a person and delegated by them under the organization's delegation, registers a record with provenance; the person and a device endorse it.

cases.name: record-key-rotations
cases.description: The log key and the root key rotated; a person's key rotated by the organization, a device's by itself; endorsements under the new keys, the checkpoint under the new log key.

cases.name: record-signer-revoked-later
cases.description: A person registers a record; later the organization revokes their delegation and the person. The record stays valid and the report shows the signer revoked.

cases.name: record-revoked
cases.description: A device registers and later revokes a record; the bundle shows the revocation.

cases.name: record-superseded
cases.description: Version 1's bundle holds the registration of version 2, which supersedes it.

cases.name: record-new-version
cases.description: Version 2's bundle, which does not hold version 1: it is checked under every rule except those about version 1.

cases.name: record-not-complete
cases.description: The checkpoint ends with a statement, not a state commitment: the bundle verifies and is not complete.

cases.name: record-commitment-left-out
cases.description: The checkpoint ends with a state commitment, which the bundle leaves out with every state proof: it verifies and is not complete.

cases.name: record-presence
cases.description: A person under a delegation that requires presence registers with a passkey (user verified), endorses with a hardware key, rotates their own key proving presence, user verified, and endorses again under the new key.

cases.name: record-witnesses
cases.description: Two cosignatures, by a trusted witness and by one the verifier does not trust.

cases.name: record-witnesses-two-trusted
cases.description: Two cosignatures by two trusted witnesses, two required.

cases.name: record-witness-counted-once
cases.description: One trusted witness's checkpoint cosigned twice (two ECDSA signatures): it counts once.

cases.name: too-few-trusted-witnesses
cases.description: Two trusted witnesses required; one trusted witness cosigned (twice), the other cosigner is not trusted.

cases.name: forged-trusted-cosignature
cases.description: The only trusted witness's cosignature does not verify (its last signature byte flipped), and one trusted witness is required.

cases.name: record-timestamp
cases.description: A trusted authority's token over the bundle's own checkpoint.

cases.name: record-timestamp-earlier-checkpoint
cases.description: A trusted token over an earlier checkpoint, with its consistency proof: the registration existed by the token's time, the later endorsement has no such bound.

cases.name: record-timestamp-two-authorities
cases.description: Tokens of two trusted authorities over the bundle's checkpoint.

cases.name: record-timestamp-one-trusted
cases.description: Tokens of two authorities, one trusted: the other is counted and relied on for nothing.

cases.name: too-few-trusted-timestamps
cases.description: Two trusted authorities required; one trusted authority stamped it.

cases.name: token-over-another-checkpoint
cases.description: An anchor holds the bundle's checkpoint with a token whose imprint is another checkpoint's payload.

cases.name: anchor-not-consistent
cases.description: An anchor's earlier checkpoint with a consistency proof that does not lead to the bundle's checkpoint.

cases.name: token-without-certificate
cases.description: A token over the bundle's checkpoint that does not carry its authority's signing certificate.

cases.name: token-imprint-other-hash
cases.description: A SHA-256 ledger's checkpoint stamped with an SM3 imprint of its payload.

cases.name: timestamp-within-clock-allowance
cases.description: The checkpoint is dated about 30 seconds after a trusted authority's time: within the 60 seconds the clock rule allows.

cases.name: clock-rule
cases.description: The ledger dates its entries and checkpoint a day after a trusted authority saw the checkpoint.

cases.name: clock-ahead-authority-not-trusted
cases.description: The same bundle, its authority not trusted: the clock rule applies only to trusted tokens.

cases.name: record-sm3-sm2
cases.description: An SM3 ledger with SM2 root, log, and signing keys, an SM2 hardware key's presence, an ESP256 witness, and a token over the SM3 hash of the checkpoint.

cases.name: record-ml-dsa
cases.description: An ML-DSA-44 person and an ESP256 device; the log key rotated to ML-DSA-65, which signs the checkpoint, the receipts, and the state commitment.

cases.name: record-consent-withdrawn
cases.description: A contract consent, given and then withdrawn by its organization.

cases.name: receipt-bad-path
cases.description: A receipt whose inclusion path has one hash changed (its signature still holds).

cases.name: receipt-other-tree-size
cases.description: One receipt proves inclusion in the tree of another size.

cases.name: entries-not-ascending
cases.description: Two entries of the bundle swapped, so their indices do not ascend.

cases.name: receipts-by-another-key
cases.description: Every receipt is signed by the person's key, not the log key.

cases.name: receipt-bad-signature
cases.description: The genesis entry's receipt signature does not verify.

cases.name: receipts-under-old-log-key
cases.description: After a log key rotation, the receipts are signed by the old log key, the checkpoint by the new.

cases.name: checkpoint-under-old-log-key
cases.description: After a log key rotation, the checkpoint is signed by the old log key, the receipts by the new.

cases.name: log-key-rotation-left-out
cases.description: The bundle leaves out the log key rotation; checkpoint and receipts are under the new key.

cases.name: root-key-rotation-left-out
cases.description: The bundle leaves out the root key rotation; the organization later signs with its new root key.

cases.name: commitment-under-old-log-key
cases.description: After a log key rotation, the state commitment is signed by the old log key.

cases.name: signer-registration-left-out
cases.description: The bundle leaves out the registration of the device that endorsed the record.

cases.name: endorsement-left-out
cases.description: The bundle leaves out an endorsement of the record.

cases.name: state-proof-left-out
cases.description: The bundle holds no state proof for the device's delegation.

cases.name: signer-revocation-left-out
cases.description: The bundle leaves out the revocation of the person who registered the record.

cases.name: record-revocation-left-out
cases.description: The bundle leaves out the record's revocation.

cases.name: disclosure-does-not-match
cases.description: A disclosed field's value changed: it does not match the field root.

cases.name: disclosure-twice
cases.description: One field disclosed twice.

cases.name: attachment-does-not-match
cases.description: An attachment opened, its content provided beside the bundle, is not the content committed to.

cases.name: wrong-ledger-id
cases.description: A verifier that expects another ledger.

cases.name: cbor-not-shortest
cases.description: The bundle encodes its format version 1 in two bytes instead of one.

cases.name: cbor-unsorted-map
cases.description: A statement whose metadata map keys are not in bytewise order, signed as such.

cases.name: scope-does-not-cover-type
cases.description: A person registers a record of a type their delegation does not list.

cases.name: delegation-expired
cases.description: A person registers a record after their delegation's not-after time.

cases.name: revoked-signer
cases.description: A person registers a record after the organization revoked them.

cases.name: revoked-delegation
cases.description: A person registers a record under a delegation revoked before.

cases.name: presence-required-missing
cases.description: A delegation requires presence; the statement carries no proof.

cases.name: presence-proof-does-not-verify
cases.description: A delegation requires presence; the hardware key signed another challenge.

cases.name: self-rotation-not-user-verified
cases.description: A person with a passkey rotates their own key with a passkey proof that is user present, not user verified.

cases.name: issued-too-late
cases.description: A statement issued 5 minutes and 1 ms after its registration time.

cases.name: agent-without-model
cases.description: An AI agent's statement whose provenance names no model (it has none).

cases.name: not-signed-by-the-signer
cases.description: A statement in the organization's name signed by a key that is not its root key.

cases.name: contract-consents
cases.description: An instance created by a registrar, made effective with the consents of a person present on a SHA-256 party ledger and of an SM3 party's organization, then closed by a clerk.

cases.name: contract-wrong-home
cases.description: The same evidence, verified for another home ledger.

cases.name: contract-require-presence-unmet
cases.description: The same evidence with presence required for every consent: the bank's organization consented without it.

cases.name: contract-consent-bundle-missing
cases.description: The evidence leaves out the bank's consent bundle, which the call cites.

cases.name: contract-consent-unpinned
cases.description: The evidence holds a consent bundle that no call cites.

cases.name: contract-not-complete
cases.description: The instance's bundle leaves out the state commitment its checkpoint ends with.

cases.name: contract-consent-terms-differ
cases.description: The consent names another function than the call's.

cases.name: contract-consent-other-arguments
cases.description: The consent names other arguments than the call's.

cases.name: contract-consent-lapsed
cases.description: The consent lapsed a minute before the call was registered.

cases.name: contract-consent-signer-claim
cases.description: The call claims the consent was signed by the organization; a person signed it, present.

cases.name: contract-consent-not-complete
cases.description: The consent's bundle does not end with a state commitment.

cases.name: contract-consent-withdrawn
cases.description: The consent was withdrawn before its bundle's checkpoint.

cases.name: contract-presence-and-retired
cases.description: A consent given by a person present with a hardware key, presence required; the contract is retired and the instance carries on.

cases.name: contract-part
cases.description: A part created by a split that cites the holder's consent, then transferred: its evidence holds its parent's calls up to the split, with that consent.

cases.name: contract-part-not-made
cases.description: Evidence for a second part of a creation whose output made one: the home's state lists it, but the replay of the code does not make it.

cases.name: contract-request-answered
cases.description: A creation makes two requests to executors; a device answers one, done, under scope keys 8 and 9; the other is open and not yet due, so --require-answered passes.

cases.name: contract-request-overdue
cases.description: A request still open three hours after its one-hour deadline, at the checkpoint: reported overdue.

cases.name: contract-overdue-require-answered
cases.description: The same evidence with --require-answered: a request is open past its deadline.
cases.rule: 15 requests in evidence (a verifier MAY fail overdue requests)

cases.name: contract-call-rejected-by-code
cases.description: The log holds a call whose contract, run again, aborts: the home recorded a call its code rejects.
cases.rule: 5 contracts, 15 ledger rules and contract evidence step 2

cases.name: contract-answer-unknown-request
cases.description: An answer to a request the creation's output never made.
cases.rule: 15 requests and answers (the request is one of the instance's, and open)

cases.name: contract-call-on-final
cases.description: A call on an instance that its creation made final.
cases.rule: 15 ledger rules (the instance is not final)

cases.name: contract-call-stale-head
cases.description: A call that names the instance's old head.
cases.rule: 15 ledger rules (the head is its head)
